title: Failure probability of the recursive learner
statement: Let $n,k$ be nonnegative integers, let a node finder for $k$-juntas on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube be given, and let $f$ be a Boolean function on that cube taking values in $\{\pm1\}$. Suppose $J$ is a set of coordinates with $|J|\le k$ on which $f$ depends, and fix a learning parameter $\varepsilon\in(0,1/2]$. For every fuel $r$, fixed-coordinate set $P\subseteq J$, and sign assignment on $P$ with $|J\setminus P|\le r$, the probability that the recursive learner fails to return a decision tree computing the restriction of $f$ consistent with that assignment is at most $T(r)\varepsilon$, where $T(0)=1$ and $T(r+1)=1+2T(r)$.
hypotheses_covered: a node finder for dimension $n$ and junta size $k$
a Boolean function $f$ on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
$J$ is a finite set of coordinates
